title: How a Thermostat Works in 60 Seconds 🌡️🔥 #shorts
description:
A classic thermostat uses a strip of two metals bonded together. They expand at different rates, so the strip bends with temperature, touches a contact and switches the furnace on or off. Digital thermostats do the same job with a thermistor and a chip. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#thermostat #heating #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: Turning your thermostat back for eight hours a day can save up to *ten percent* a year on heating and cooling.

steps.label: Strip
steps.text: Classic thermostats use a *bimetallic strip*, two metals bonded together.

steps.label: Bend
steps.text: The metals expand at *different rates*, so the strip *bends* as the room warms or cools.

steps.label: Contact
steps.text: When the room gets cold, the strip touches a *contact* and closes a circuit.

steps.label: Furnace
steps.text: That signal tells the *furnace* to fire up and blow *warm air*.

steps.label: Digital
steps.text: Digital thermostats use a *thermistor* and a chip instead, but the loop is the same.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Sense, bend, *switch*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
